rationale: Genesis WorkflowEngine is currently evidenced as an in-process Python API with an injected Executor; no established remote or IPC API is evidenced.
A process boundary permits explicit schema validation, resource limits, cancellation and auditable lifecycle without introducing a network service as a prerequisite.
The ecosystem repository records the contract only; adapter implementation belongs to aurora-ai and engine-native workflow execution remains owned by genesis-engine.
transport_decision.protocol: UTF-8 JSON Lines over supervised stdin/stdout; one complete JSON object per line; stdout is protocol-only; diagnostics go to stderr.
transport_decision.isolation: Dedicated unprivileged child process or container, ephemeral workspace, read-only engine/toolchain inputs where possible, bounded writable output directory, network denied by default, no inherited secrets or ambient credentials.
transport_decision.fallback: Do not silently fall back to in-process imports or network transport. Any future service/IPC transport requires a new ADR and compatible contract version.
transport_decision.limitation: This is an architecture decision for the first integration milestone, not evidence that a working adapter exists.

capability_token_ref.description: Opaque reference resolved by the trusted local authorization broker; never a bearer secret embedded in logs.

security_invariants: Deny by default; Aurora-generated plans are proposals, not authorization.
Authenticate caller workload identity independently of model-provided fields; bind identity to the exact Aurora build SHA.
Authorize each operation and workflow against a server-side allowlist and capability policy; never trust capability names supplied in the request as proof of authority.
Approval is bound to request hash, workflow ID/version, artifact destination and side-effect class; reject missing, expired, replayed or mismatched approvals.
Enforce absolute deadline and maximum timeout at the supervisor; cancellation is idempotent, acknowledged and escalates to process termination after a short grace period.
Use idempotency keys for mutating operations; retries must return the original terminal result or explicitly report a conflict, never silently execute twice.

Record append-only audit events for accepted/rejected request, identity, policy decision, approval, capability decision, start/step/end, timeout/cancel, artifact hash/validation, exit status and exact source SHAs.
Redact secrets and sensitive input from logs; logs are bounded and access-controlled; audit records include content hashes/references instead of bearer tokens.
Validate the artifact schema, path containment, size limit, content digest and provenance before returning SUCCEEDED; invalid or missing artifact means no success.
No network access, repository writes, commits, pushes, deployments or external publication without separately granted capability and required human approval.
lifecycle: Aurora validates the request locally and resolves caller identity.
Authorization broker validates identity, capability, policy decision, approval and deadline; default deny on any uncertainty.
Supervisor launches or reuses only a pinned isolated adapter worker and sends the JSONL request.
Genesis resolves the exact allowlisted workflow/version, validates input and executes within resource limits.
Genesis emits a typed result; adapter validates artifact schema/hash/provenance and normalizes errors.
Supervisor enforces timeout/cancellation, captures bounded stdout/stderr and process exit code, and writes audit events.
Aurora validates response correlation, status, artifact digest and audit reference before exposing the result.

acceptance_tests.name: consequential operation without matching approval denied
deadline expires and worker is terminated
cancel request is acknowledged and execution stops
duplicate idempotency key does not duplicate mutation
tampered or invalid artifact never returns SUCCEEDED
audit event chain contains request/capability/approval/step/exit/artifact hash and pinned SHAs

flow: Aurora submits a deterministic fixture workflow request
authorization and capability check allow the fixture operation
artifact is validated and SHA-256 computed
typed response is returned to Aurora and correlation/artifact/audit references are checked
required_evidence: exact commit SHA for ecosystem contract
e2e_test.pass_criteria: All required evidence exists for the same pinned source revisions; the artifact is validated; the workflow and process exit codes are zero; negative authorization/timeout/cancellation tests pass.

residuals: No adapter implementation is established by current evidence.
Aurora runtime tool executor and sandbox are marked PLANNED in COMPONENT_PLAN.md.
The exact current default-branch HEADs and active Genesis workflow/artifact source paths still require live reconciliation.
The schema is a normative proposal; schema validation and compatibility tests have not been run.
No end-to-end run, Run-ID, Job-ID, Step-ID, exit code or terminal logs have been captured.
